_comment: Example provider registry config for pkgs/idp-provider (Slice 3, #13409; doors #13411/#13412/#13414; linking #13415). The REAL config lives on-host with the provider (point IDP_PROVIDER_CONFIG at it) and is never committed: it carries the owner's credential HASH. Generate the hash on-host with `IDP_LOCAL_CREDENTIAL=... idp-provider hash-credential`. An empty hash verifies nothing, so this example cannot open the door. Door client ids below are placeholders; door client SECRETS are never in this file — each door names the environment variable the launcher fills from the vault by name (idp.github.client-secret -> IDP_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, idp.google.client-secret -> IDP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, idp.microsoft.client-secret -> IDP_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET). A door whose secret env is unset stays disabled. Door endpoints and the Microsoft issuer (the consumers tenant id segment) must be checked against the actual app registrations when they are created. The account.identities list is the identity store's seed; link state after first boot lives in identity_db_path.
_saml_comment: Static SAML SP trust (#13793). No metadata is fetched. entity_id is exact/opaque; acs_urls must be HTTPS (HTTP only for loopback). request_signing_certificate is optional PEM X.509; require_signed_requests needs one. released_attributes defaults to roles + displayName; [] releases neither. This localhost example is only for local testing, not a real SP registration.
